notes: Results-day run (FE_LAG_DAYS=0). Read-only review of casefile.json, position.json, understand/business.json, prefetch/forensic.json, gather/macro.json and evidence_pack.json. expectation_gap was run independently (fundamental_engine.expectations.expectation_gap) with a base-like anchor built from position.json. The capital structure used: cash 55.9bn; spendable securities 106.6bn; restricted SpaceX plus non-marketable stakes 211.5bn at the module's default 25% haircut; debt 100.16bn; mandatory convertible preferred 19.25bn; 12.23bn shares. The anchor: FY2027 revenue 599bn on FY2026 498bn, growth 18% for 3 years fading to 4.49%, margin 31%, tax 16%, Ke 9.44%, sales-to-capital 0.52, terminal ROIC 0.31. Scratch script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/3d8b7c18-0191-53bf-8156-d4cdcae7ee35/scratchpad/eg.py. redteam_audit was not run because the run has no capital_bridge package (no reported/events block). Its debt_complete check was applied by hand (finding ct3).

findings.where: position.json drivers.sales_to_capital.base (0.52) -> casefile val.result.scenarios[base].forecast (capex 2027 about 211.5bn = maintenance 31.4 + growth 180.1; 2028 213.2; 2029 211.2) vs rp_g_capex_fy26_oct / rp_call_20261028 ('increase significantly in 2027'); casefile val.diagnostics.stress.stresses
findings.finding: The 'cheap by about 21%' result does not survive the company's own guidance. The base keeps total capex roughly flat at about 211bn a year for 2027-2029. That is only about +5% over the FY2026 guide midpoint of 200bn, while management guided capex to 'increase significantly in 2027', and capex is the only metric Alphabet guides. The engine's own stresses all return funding_blocked from 2026-12-31 in base and bear: capex +25%, cash costs +15% and prices -20%. So the base cannot be valued under the very path management guided. An independent expectation_gap driver model with base-like anchors gives about 301 per share (+3% vs 291.96), not 367. With sales-to-capital 0.42 (capex about +25%) it gives 273. With the company's incremental return on new capital (terminal ROIC 0.20, prefetch/forensic.json roic.incremental_roic 0.218, see company_first cf1) it gives 277. With both it gives about 249, 15% BELOW the price. The sign of the verdict, not just its size, depends on two inputs where the company's own evidence points against the base.
findings.fix: Set the 2027-2028 investment path to the guidance. Use a lower base sales_to_capital for 2027-28 (about 0.40-0.45), or an explicit capex path at least 20-25% above 200bn in 2027, unless the call or 10-Q gives a number; cite rp_call_20261028. Model the funding the company actually uses: notes at market coupons, the ATM and the preferred. The funding_blocked stresses must then resolve. Apply the incremental-RONIC fix from company_first cf1. Rerun ticker-value and show the new discount. Until then the table cannot say 'זולה בכ-21%'.

findings.where: counter-thesis (pre-mortem), for review/counter_thesis.json and the deliver notes; ties to position.json key_risk, scenario_events.bear
findings.finding: Pre-mortem: by October 2029 the investment has failed because Alphabet became a capital-heavy AI utility. Its core ad monopoly is decaying, so it trades on a utility multiple. (1) Services keeps sliding (16% -> 14.5% -> 10.6% in 2026; Search 19% -> 12%) while Meta grows ads +25.9%. AI assistants and the Search remedies erode query share, so Services, about 70% of revenue and 78% of segment profit, grows at mid-single digits. (2) The Cloud backlog (561bn, from a third-party call copy, concentration undisclosed) is dominated by a few AI labs. They are funded partly by Alphabet's own backstops (up to 43.8bn credit derivatives, 24.1bn agreed, 20bn milestone funding) and by its own private stakes. When their funding tightens, conversion slips and some contracts are renegotiated. (3) The capex roughly doubled (200bn in 2026, 'significantly' more in 2027) and the 924bn of purchase commitments are fixed. Depreciation (+49% y/y already) arrives on time; revenue does not. Operating margin falls back to the 2022-23 26-27%, and the return on the 2026-27 capital stays at the 13-15% seen so far. (4) The financing turns a net-cash buyback story into a diluting borrower. Debt went from 46.5bn to 125.1bn in nine months; there are no buybacks in 2026, an ATM (27.6bn left), a 49.6bn June raise and a mandatory convertible converting in 2029. (5) The private marks (SpaceX, one private company) that inflated 2026 GAAP EPS reverse; Q3 already had -8.2bn of other income. The market then pays 14-18x (own-history low 15.2) for EPS that barely grows, so the price ends near the bear's 190-215. What would have shown it early: Services growth below 8% in any 2027 quarter; Cloud backlog additions below about 20bn a quarter (they were about 47-52bn); 2027 capex guided above 250bn without a matching revenue step-up; Cloud operating margin falling back below 30%; another ATM or equity issue; quarterly FCF negative for a third quarter; a disclosed backstop draw or a 10-Q note naming a major customer.
findings.fix: Carry this paragraph in the deliver notes as the counter-thesis. Turn the early signals into the numeric falsifiers named in ct8.

findings.where: casefile val.case.opening {debt 119.414bn incl. 19.25bn preferred, shares 12.23bn, marketable_investments 318.024bn} + assumptions 'bridge' ('No bridge events applied between 2026-06-30 and 2026-10-28') and 'claims' ('No preferred stock ... recorded') vs evidence_pack nm_long_term_debt_q_2026_09_30 (125.102bn), nm_debt_issuance_net_proceeds_q_2026_09_30 (28.996bn), nm_shares_outstanding_q_2026_09_30 (12.294bn), nm_equity_issuance_net_proceeds_atm_q_2026_09_30 (12.371bn), nm_other_income_net_q_2026_09_30 (-8.221bn), nm_non_marketable_securities_q_2026_09_30 (135.23bn)
findings.finding: The red-team capital check fails. The valuation opens on the 2026-06-30 balance sheet with no bridge, though the 2026-09-30 balance sheet is in the cited release. Straight debt in the model is 100.16bn against 125.1bn of long-term debt at 9/30 after 29.0bn of new notes in Q3. Shares are 12.230bn against 12.294bn after the 12.4bn ATM. The investments are carried at their 6/30 marks although Q3 booked -8.2bn of other income, mostly mark losses, while non-marketable securities moved to 135.2bn. The 'claims' assumption still says no preferred stock is recorded while the opening adds the 19.25bn preferred: the two rows contradict each other. redteam_audit's debt_complete check, a critical check, would FAIL with the Q3 issuance as a dated post-statement event. The value effect is probably modest (roughly -1 to -3% if the cash raised went into capex and private stakes) but unsigned until bridged. The debt is also carried at a 1.00% coupon: interest about 1.2bn a year on 119.4bn, while the preferred dividend alone is 1.19bn a year (298m a quarter) and the Q3 notes were issued at market rates. This understates interest in every company_path EPS.
findings.fix: Re-open the case on the 2026-09-30 balance sheet from pf_rel_20261028_1: cash 56.3bn, debt including current, preferred, shares 12.294bn, marketable and non-marketable securities. If any line is missing, apply dated bridge events for the Q3 notes, ATM, FCF and other income. Correct the 'claims' assumption text. Set the debt coupon from the debt note (blended, with the 2026 issues at their stated coupons) and keep the 6.25% preferred dividend as a claim cost. Build the capital_bridge package and run redteam_audit.

findings.where: casefile val.case.opening.marketable_investments 318.024bn; assumption 'investment_income' (risk-free 4.99% on all 318bn); assumption 'open_balance' ('private stakes at book value only'); understand/business.json flag restricted_not_spendable; dc_marketable_equity_q2_2026; dc_nonmarketable_securities_q2_2026
findings.finding: About 26 per share (7% of the 367 base value) comes from investments counted at face. They include 80.0bn of SpaceX shares under sale restrictions (plus 14.1bn more restricted through Q3 2027) and 131.5-135.2bn of non-marketable stakes. Those stakes were marked up mainly on one private company (99.0bn of unrealized gains in Q2 2026, 36.9bn in Q1). The 22.8bn deferred tax liability created by those marks is not deducted. The stakes are also credited the 4.99% risk-free rate as income (about 12.5bn a year after tax in base), though equity stakes pay nothing. That income flows into the company_path EPS (bear FY2027 EPS 12.69 includes about 11.4bn of investment income) and is then multiplied by the P/E. The business file itself says these stakes 'are not liquidity'. The bear is an AI and capital-market overbuild that would hit exactly these private AI and space marks, yet it does not haircut them.
findings.fix: Separate the investments into debt securities and spendable equity at face (about 106.6bn) and restricted or non-marketable stakes. Apply a haircut to the second group (capital.summarize applies 25% by default to long_term_investments) and a deeper one in the bear (e.g. -50%). Deduct the deferred tax liability on unrealized gains. Credit investment income only on the interest-bearing part.

findings.where: casefile val.what_must_be_true (mature_margin: not_reachable, range_values [367.419, 770.30]; capital_efficiency: not_reachable, range_values [490.15, 367.417]) and analyst_sheet mispricing (price_needs_growth 8.4%)
findings.finding: What the price already assumes is misreported. The engine says no mature margin from 6% to 61%, and no capex scaling from 0x to 6x, can bring the base down to the price. Its own range values show why: the downside end of each search returns the unchanged base value (367.42). The levers are inert at the downside, probably because the driver spec's explicit margin and capital paths override them. The independent expectation_gap run, each lever alone from a base-like anchor, says the opposite. The price is reconciled by a mature margin of 30.3% (anchor 31%, best of the last 3 years 32.1%) or by sales-to-capital of 0.48 (anchor 0.52, 2026 guide-implied about 0.56). Growth needs only a slightly lower level: 17.0% vs 18% for the high-growth years, a 5y revenue CAGR of about 15.6% against 12.5% demonstrated over 3 years (evidence_below_requirement). So the price already assumes roughly the base case, not 8.4% growth. With a terminal RONIC of 0.20, all three levers move to evidence_below_requirement (growth 20%, margin 32.3%, sales-to-capital 0.60).
findings.fix: In the deliver text, do not say that margins or capex cannot explain the price. Report the independent reading: the price is consistent with the base drivers, and small shortfalls in margin or capital efficiency close the gap. Flag the inert margin and capital_efficiency levers of val.what_must_be_true as an engine issue for the owner (outside this run's scope).

findings.where: position.json scenario_events.base[2] ('funded from operating cash flow, debt and the ATM (27.6bn left)') and scenario_events.bear[3] (debt 46.5 -> 125.1bn, no buybacks, ATM, shares +1.7%) vs casefile val.result.scenarios[*].forecast (shares 12.23bn and debt 119.4bn constant in every year of every scenario; new_financing_shares 0; investment_liquidation 26.5bn + 18.4bn in bear funds the gap)
findings.finding: The bear does not change funding. Its events describe dilution and borrowing as a mechanism; its numbers keep shares and debt flat forever and fund the 2026-27 shortfall by selling investments. The base has the same incoherence. The 'financing weighs on shareholders' leg of the bear is therefore narrative only. The bear does change growth (FY2027 +11%, then 7-10%), margin (to 26%) and capital intensity (sales-to-capital 0.30), so it is more than a multiple cut; the funding leg is the missing one. Contingent exposures named in the bear (backstops up to 43.8bn, 24.1bn agreed, 20bn private-company funding) and an AI-lab customer failure have no cash or revenue line either: the bear Cloud still grows +30% to 145bn.
findings.fix: Bear: add the ATM remainder (27.6bn) and new notes at market coupons as financing. Add a sized backstop draw (cap 43.8 + 24.1 + 20.0bn, or a stated share of it, labelled hypothesis because concentration is undisclosed). Add a backlog cancellation or slip tied to the undisclosed-concentration gap. Base: either model the ATM use the base event names, or delete it from the event.

findings.where: casefile rk.register biz.regulation (pricing_status not_priced, in_bear_case false), dil.sbc (not_priced), exe.stress_funding_gap (not_priced); understand/business.json flags sbc_rising, other_bets_losses_widening, legal_regulatory; assumption sbc_path (SBC fades 20% over 5 years)
findings.finding: Several forensic and business flags are missing from the bear and the priced risks. (a) SBC is 6.8% of revenue in Q3, +36% y/y, while the model fades it 20% in every scenario, the bear included; it is an engine default with no company evidence. (b) Other Bets losses widened to 2.05bn a quarter (from 1.43bn) and appear in no scenario. (c) The US Search remedies touch about half of revenue and are on cross-appeal. The bear mentions them but does not size them, and the register marks them not priced. (d) The engine's own funding stress is not priced. Piotroski 7/8 and Altman safe are fine; Beneish is unavailable, which is a gap.
findings.fix: Bear: hold SBC at 6.8% of revenue or rising, not fading. Carry the Other Bets loss run-rate (about 8bn a year) or show it is inside the margin path. Size the Search remedy as a Services growth or margin haircut, labelled hypothesis, or keep it as a visible unsized gap in the risk row. Record Beneish as unavailable in the risks.

findings.where: position.json falsifiers (fx_services_q2_27 threshold 0.06; no base falsifier on capex, FCF or margin)
findings.finding: The falsifiers do not test the key risk. The key risk is capex and fixed commitments outrunning revenue, yet no base falsifier covers margin, capex or FCF. The base Services falsifier triggers only below 6% growth, though the base assumes +10% and the bear +5%: the base is refuted only once the bear has nearly happened.
findings.fix: Raise fx_services_q2_27 to about 0.08. Add base falsifiers on Alphabet GAAP operating margin for FY2027 below 0.29 (by 2028-02-15) and on FY2027 capex above about 250bn while FY2027 Cloud revenue is below about 165bn (by 2028-02-15). Add quarterly Cloud backlog additions below 20bn for two straight quarters (by 2027-08-15).

findings.where: casefile company_path.scenarios.bull (multiple_path 45.0, 39.0, 34.8 ...; year-1 value 778 = +166%) vs company_path.own_history {low 15.2, median 17.4, high 31.8}; position.json drivers.growth_anchor.bull (+30%, Cloud 210bn)
findings.finding: The bull path's first three years sit above the company's own forward P/E record: 45x today, 39x and 35x against a 2021-24 high of 31.8x. Bull revenue reaches about 1.19 trillion by 2030 (about 2.4x FY2026), and bull FY2027 Cloud (210bn) exceeds what the disclosed backlog converts (about 154bn a year). A +166% one-year bull price and a +268% five-year bull shown in the headline row invite reading the bull as reachable. It is labelled 'unproven', which is right, but nothing in the table says the multiple is above anything the company has traded at.
findings.fix: In the table's condition line for שורי, say that its multiple is above the company's 2021-24 high (31.8x). Or justify the economics-mode ROIC 0.29 against the 13-22% incremental record. Relabel the bull growth-anchor tier as hypothesis (see company_first cf2).

findings.where: casefile val.case.quote (291.96, ib:snapshot, after-hours); position.json drivers.growth_anchor evidence rp_call_20261028 / web:ex_call_q3_2026 (retrieval search_excerpt)
findings.finding: Two inputs of this results-day run are provisional. The quote is a thin after-hours print after a reported profit miss and about a 10% drop; the discount and the buy-below row will move at the 2026-10-29 open. The backlog (561bn), 55%/24m conversion and 924bn commitments, which carry both the base growth and the key risk, come from an AI-assisted third-party copy of the call, not an issuer document (company_first cf3). The ad-recession bear event has no evidence ids and is correctly labelled a hypothesis.
findings.fix: State both in the deliver notes. Rerun with the 2026-10-29 close and the Q3 10-Q once filed.
